newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude steepens declines late session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude steepens declines late session.

text.p: NYMEX crude sharpened its losses Monday late session as oil prices sagged under ample supplies in the U.S. Gulf and sent prompt crude into a decisive contango, traders said.
"This (contango) could be a temporary blip while the crude is assimilated," said Pat Hughes, market analyst with Chevron Corp in Walnut Creek, Calif.
At 1505 EST, April crude was off 71 cents a barrel at $20.57. April heating oil was off 0.78 cent at 53.30 cents while April gasoline was off 1.37 cent at 64.30 cents a gallon.
Some traders said weekly oil inventory data by the American Petroleum Institute (API) may not rescue spot crude from contango even if there is a bullish draw in crude stocks.

"The cash market spreads have really weakened. Even if the APIs are good, it may take more than that to turn this market around," said a New York crude trader, noting crude runs would have to increase for an extended period to absorb the excess crude.
Traders said the April gasoline-to-crude crack, which stood at $6.61 a barrel, its highest level in more than a year, was providing strong incentive to produce gasoline.
"I know we are going to produce as much gasoline as we can as soon as we get out of turnaround," said one source at a major refiner who requested anonymity.

Crude runs are expected to increase anyway as refiners typically focus on gasoline output in the spring to meet demand for the summer driving season. But, analysts said a rise in crude supply from OPEC countries, such as Iraq, could offset the increase in crude runs.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
